questions.question: Inequalities $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i$, $i=1,\dots,N$, are modelled as $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+My_i$ ($i=1,\dots,N$) with binary $y_i$, a valid big-M constant $M$, and $\sum_{i=1}^{N}y_i\le N-K$, where $0\le K\le N$. What does this formulation guarantee about $\boldsymbol{x}$?
options: Exactly $K$ of the $N$ original inequalities hold.
At least $K$ of the $N$ original inequalities hold.
At most $K$ of the $N$ original inequalities hold.
Exactly $N-K$ of the original inequalities are violated.

questions.question: In the K-out-of-N formulation $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+My_i$ ($i=1,\dots,N$) with binary $y_i$, a valid big-M constant $M$, and $\sum_{i=1}^{N}y_i\le N-K$, what does $y_3=1$ mean for the third inequality $\boldsymbol{a}_3^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_3$?
options: It must be violated by the chosen $\boldsymbol{x}$.
It is released: it may hold or fail, as $M$ removes it.
It is enforced, since $y_3=1$ means 'yes, impose it'.
It is deleted, so $\boldsymbol{x}$ no longer enters it.

questions.question: In the K-out-of-N formulation $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+My_i$ ($i=1,\dots,N$) with binary $y_i$, a valid big-M constant $M$, and $\sum_{i=1}^{N}y_i\le N-K$, why is the right-hand side of the selector constraint $N-K$?
options: At most $N-K$ releases leave at least $K$ inequalities enforced.
At most $K$ releases make exactly $K$ inequalities relaxed.
Any of the $N$ inequalities may be released, as $M$ is valid.
$N-K$ is the number of inequalities that must be violated.

questions.question: In the K-out-of-N formulation $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+My_i$ ($i=1,\dots,N$) with binary $y_i$, a valid big-M constant $M$, and $\sum_{i=1}^{N}y_i\le N-K$, the modeller sets $K=0$. What does the formulation then require of $\boldsymbol{x}$?
options: All $N$ inequalities must hold.
At least one of the inequalities must hold.
Nothing: all $N$ inequalities may be released together.
No $\boldsymbol{x}$ is feasible, as no inequality is required.

questions.question: A model releases inequality $i$ through $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+My_i$ when the binary $y_i$ is 1, with release budget $\sum_iy_i\le N-K$. Now every one of the $N$ inequalities is required, so $K=N$. What does the model do?
options: Exactly one inequality may be released.
No inequality may be released, so all $N$ must hold.
Any number of inequalities may be released.
The value of $M$ now decides which inequalities hold.

questions.question: At least two of three constraints must hold. Each constraint $i$ is written as $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+My_i$ with binary release indicator $y_i$ (1 = released) and a valid $M$. Which constraint on $y_1,y_2,y_3$ completes the model?

At least three of five constraints must hold. Each constraint $i$ is written as $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+My_i$ with binary release indicator $y_i$ (1 = released) and a valid $M$. Which selector constraint is correct?
options: $y_1+\dots+y_5\le2$
$y_1+\dots+y_5\le3$
$y_1+\dots+y_5\ge3$
$y_1+\dots+y_5\le5$

questions.question: Continuous $x_1,x_2\ge0$ must satisfy at least two of the three inequalities $x_1+x_2\le6$, $x_1\le3$ and $x_2\le2$. Which point $(x_1,x_2)$ is feasible?

For $0\le x_1,x_2\le10$, the constraints $2x_1+x_2\le8+My_1$, $x_1\le3+My_2$, $x_2\le4+My_3$ with $M=30$, binary $y_i$ (1 = released) and $y_1+y_2+y_3\le1$ are given. Which selector vector $(y_1,y_2,y_3)$ makes $\boldsymbol{x}=(3.5,1)$ feasible?

Variables satisfy $0\le x_1\le5$ and $0\le x_2\le5$. The inequality $x_1+x_2\le4$ is to be released through $x_1+x_2\le4+My$, $y\in\{0,1\}$. What is the smallest $M$ for which the released form never cuts off a point of this box?

The either-or formulation $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le b+My$, $\boldsymbol{d}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le e+M(1-y)$ with $y\in\{0,1\}$ requires at least one of two inequalities. Which K-out-of-N formulation, with $\sum_iy_i\le N-K$, does the same?
options: $N=2$, $K=2$: no release is allowed
$N=1$, $K=1$: a single inequality
$N=2$, $K=0$: both may be released
$N=2$, $K=1$: at most one release

questions.question: A modeller writes $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+M(1-z_i)$ for $i=1,\dots,N$, with binary $z_i$ and a valid $M$, so that $z_i=1$ means 'enforced'. Which constraint on the $z_i$ requires at least $K$ inequalities to hold?
options: $\sum_{i=1}^{N}z_i\ge K$
$\sum_{i=1}^{N}z_i\le N-K$
$\sum_{i=1}^{N}z_i\le K$
$\sum_{i=1}^{N}z_i\ge N-K$

questions.question: In the K-out-of-N formulation $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+My_i$ ($i=1,\dots,N$) with binary $y_i$, a constant $M$, and $\sum_{i=1}^{N}y_i\le N-K$, the chosen $M$ is smaller than needed for the variable bounds. What can go wrong?
options: Points violating more than $N-K$ inequalities become feasible.
Nothing, since $M$ only needs to be positive.
Released inequalities still bind and cut off allowed points.
The selector constraint must then use $N$ instead of $N-K$.

questions.question: One of three constraints in an at-least-2-of-3 requirement is $3x_1+x_2\ge6$, with $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Using a binary release indicator $y$ (1 = released) and a valid $M>0$, how should this $\ge$ constraint be written?
A single variable $x\ge0$ must satisfy at least three of the four upper bounds $x\le2$, $x\le5$, $x\le9$ and $x\le12$. What is the largest feasible value of $x$?

For $0\le x_1,x_2\le10$ and the inequalities $x_1+x_2\le6$, $x_1\le3$, $x_2\le2$, each relaxed by $+20y_i$ with binary $y_i$, a modeller wanting at least two to hold writes $y_1+y_2+y_3\ge1$ instead of $\le1$. Which point becomes feasible although it should not be?

Inequalities $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i$ on continuous $\boldsymbol{x}\ge\boldsymbol{0}$ with no upper bounds are to be released via $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+My_i$. One of them is $x_1-x_2\le3$, and nothing else in the model bounds $x_1$. What is true about $M$ for this inequality?
options: A very large value such as $M=10^6$ releases it fully.
$M=3$ suffices, matching the right-hand side.
No $M$ is needed, since $x_2$ can grow to offset $x_1$.
No finite $M$ releases it fully, since $x_1-x_2$ is unbounded.

questions.question: A modeller wants exactly two of three inequalities to hold and the third to fail. She writes $\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le d_i+My_i$ with valid $M$, binary $y_i$, and $y_1+y_2+y_3=1$. Does this enforce her requirement?
options: Yes: exactly one release means exactly one inequality fails.
No: the equality makes the model infeasible for every $\boldsymbol{x}$.
No: the released inequality may still hold, so all three may hold.
Yes, provided $M$ is chosen as small as possible.

questions.question: For $0\le x_1,x_2\le6$, at least one of $x_1\le2$ and $x_2\le2$ must hold. The model uses $x_1\le2+3y_1$, $x_2\le2+3y_2$, $y_1+y_2\le1$, binary $y_i$, so $M=3$ is too small. Which point that meets the requirement is wrongly excluded?

For $0\le x_1,x_2\le10$, maximize $x_1+x_2$ subject to at least two of the three constraints $x_1\le4$, $x_2\le3$, $x_1+x_2\le5$, using release indicators with $y_1+y_2+y_3\le1$ and a valid $M$. What is the optimal value?
